subject.title: Plugin Hooks: Missing trace context for observability (messageId, runId in all hooks, parentSpanId)

question: Should OpenClaw standardize plugin trace correlation through a narrow typed trace-context contract, or should it add the requested run/message/span fields broadly to every legacy and modern hook?
rationale: Both paths affect the public plugin SDK, identifier exposure, deprecated before_agent_start semantics, outbound delivery hooks, and subagent lifecycle contracts; automation cannot safely choose the permanent API shape.

options.title: Design narrow trace contract
options.body: Use the existing DiagnosticTraceContext and typed lifecycle hooks as the canonical observability surface, then add only the missing run/message/subagent fields required to make that contract complete.

options.title: Add broad fields everywhere
options.body: Treat the issue literally by adding runId/messageId/senderId/span fields across all applicable hook payloads and contexts, accepting a larger public SDK expansion.

options.title: Defer to narrower issues
options.body: Leave this umbrella open only as context and handle outbound runId, agent_start, and sender metadata through the existing narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Design narrow trace contract
recommendation.body: Use the existing DiagnosticTraceContext and typed lifecycle hooks as the canonical observability surface, then add only the missing run/message/subagent fields required to make that contract complete.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the recent diagnostic trace carrier and plugin hook contract split most directly tied to the API direction.
